title: Sync with Stakeholders at Work
coreMove: Make your planned work visible to stakeholders before silence gets misread as neglect or availability.
sourcePressure: The chapter closes traction by protecting work time through explicit alignment with people whose expectations can otherwise become interruptions.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: A weak run would preach focus at work without negotiating the expectations that make focus possible.

hook: Sync with Stakeholders at Work as a labeled topic opener
counterintuition: phones are not the problem by itself
tryThisNow: set a timer and notice your distractions
examples: reused old-package object-anchor shell from earlier Indistractable run

exampleSpecs.domain: regional blood-bank scheduler coordinating hospital calls
exampleSpecs.audience: scheduler whose quiet planning block looks like nonresponse
exampleSpecs.stakes: hospitals need clarity without constant interruption
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she sends the triage window and emergency channel before starting the allocation board
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A blood-type allocation board sits beside a red emergency line card.

exampleSpecs.domain: animation producer aligning directors before a render review
exampleSpecs.audience: producer who gets pinged for every tiny status question
exampleSpecs.stakes: render time is wasted by unclear review expectations
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he posts the review order, silence window, and escalation rule before locking the render queue
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A storyboard strip sits beside a render-queue dashboard.

exampleSpecs.domain: public-health analyst preparing a county dashboard
exampleSpecs.audience: analyst whose commissioners expect instant revisions
exampleSpecs.stakes: bad numbers spread if draft time is continually broken
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she shares a two-hour validation block and a noon correction cutoff with the commissioners
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A county heat map is pinned under a correction cutoff note.

exampleSpecs.domain: ship repair estimator working across foremen and owners
exampleSpecs.audience: estimator caught between yard questions and client pressure
exampleSpecs.stakes: bid accuracy fails when every party assumes immediate answers
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he creates one visible estimate window and one urgent-damage channel before measuring hull plates
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A hull-plate gauge lies beside an estimate window sheet.

exampleSpecs.domain: literary agent reading a contract for a debut novelist
exampleSpecs.audience: agent whose client worries silence means bad news
exampleSpecs.stakes: rushed reading can miss rights language
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before, the client sends anxious nudges; after, the agent sets a read block and update time
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A rights clause is highlighted beside a fountain-pen cap.

exampleSpecs.domain: construction safety officer planning a crane lift review
exampleSpecs.audience: officer whose radio keeps pulling him off the lift plan
exampleSpecs.stakes: crew risk rises if stakeholder needs are not routed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he tells the superintendent when he is unreachable and who handles non-lift questions
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A crane lift diagram is clipped beneath a radio channel card.
